subject.title: Surface internal system messages in a distinct UI block instead of normal chat bubbles

question: Should OpenClaw hide agent-only internal/runtime turns, render intentionally visible runtime notices in a dedicated diagnostic/system block, or keep the current normal chat projection for visible notices?
rationale: The remaining work is not the fixed memory-flush leak; it is a product/API choice about runtime audience and UI semantics across multiple surfaces.

options.title: Audience Contract First
options.body: Define agent-only versus visible-diagnostic provenance in Gateway/session projection, then render visible diagnostics distinctly in Control UI/WebChat and TUI.

options.title: UI-Only Diagnostic Block
options.body: Render existing system-role rows in a separate visual block without changing the runtime audience contract, accepting the risk that agent-only internals may still be exposed.

options.title: No Product Change
options.body: Keep current hidden-internal cleanup plus normal chat rendering for intentionally visible notices, and narrow or close this issue accordingly.

recommendation.title: Audience Contract First
recommendation.body: Define agent-only versus visible-diagnostic provenance in Gateway/session projection, then render visible diagnostics distinctly in Control UI/WebChat and TUI.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision crosses Control UI rendering and Gateway projection, where steipete has the strongest recent routing signal in the inspected history.
